name: Realms
description: Private Linux desktops for agents, shared by a thread and its verified subagents: a lightweight labwc Realm or an Omarchy QEMU/KVM guest with its own kernel and disk. Explicit file copies, private capture and input; ordinary coding stays on the host. Optional test tools only; ordinary provider shell/files/other tools are unaffected. There is nothing to exit.

actions.title: Realm: manage this thread's private desktop
actions.description: Manage this thread's private desktop. Input: {action: on|off|status|size|stop|repair|shot|watch, kind?: "realm"|"omarchy-vm", size?: "WIDTHxHEIGHT"}. on honors a named kind, otherwise reuses the thread preference; switching stops current compute and keeps both workspaces. Omarchy VM setup requires a person's reviewed approval (signed ISO ~5 GiB, plugin-local base and driver). off revokes agent use; stop ends compute and keeps data. VM stopped disks expire after the configured retention (14 days, 0 keeps). repair resets only the GUI connection; take a fresh capture and never replay uncertain input. shot returns an image. Status includes selected kind. Never substitute the physical desktop. A person's Off and human takeover exclude agent use. Verified subagents use the parent’s Realm; forks have their own. Omit thread overrides, coordinate shared-screen input, and respect Off and human takeover. Realm actions only; ordinary host tools are unaffected, so continue ordinary work.

actions.title: Realm: run a command inside this thread's desktop
actions.description: Run a command in this thread's selected Realm. Input: {command, cwd?: absolute target path, background?: boolean, timeoutSeconds?: number up to 20} or {jobId, signal?: INT|TERM|KILL|HUP}. Use background for GUI apps. Regular Realms share host files/network but use a private display and buses. Omarchy VM commands run as the guest desktop user over generation-pinned SSH, with guest environment and no host credentials, mounts, agent or X11 forwarding. Host paths are not guest paths; use realm-files for explicit copies. Poll jobs by jobId. Physical desktop access is refused; never work around human control. Ordinary builds/git remain in the normal host shell. Verified subagents use the parent’s Realm; forks have their own. Omit thread overrides, coordinate shared-screen input, and respect Off and human takeover. Realm actions only; ordinary host tools are unaffected, so continue ordinary work.

actions.title: Realm: see and control apps in this thread's desktop
actions.description: Computer use inside this thread's Realm through the pinned GUI driver. Input: {tool, arguments?}. tool "list" shows the available tools, "describe:<name>" a tool's arguments. get_desktop_state returns a screenshot image; list_apps and get_window_state (accessibility tree with element tokens) find apps; list_windows only sees X11 windows, so native Wayland apps may be missing there; click, type_text, press_key, hotkey, scroll and drag act on those apps. Verify the app's actual state after input; a successful response alone is not proof. Never acts on the physical desktop. For omarchy-vm the driver runs inside the guest over pinned SSH. Initial staging is a detached job and can return starting; retry after status, without replaying input. Verified subagents use the parent’s Realm; forks have their own. Omit thread overrides, coordinate shared-screen input, and respect Off and human takeover. Realm actions only; ordinary host tools are unaffected, so continue ordinary work.

actions.title: Realm: copy selected files to or from the VM
actions.description: Explicit Omarchy VM file copies. {action:"push", source: absolute host path, destination?: absolute guest path} or {action:"pull", source: absolute guest path, destination: required absolute host path}. Omitted push destination is the guest user's home plus source basename. Paths are literal: no globbing, implicit project sync or host mounts. Directory push selects the exact guest directory; pull into an existing directory treats it as a container. Different existing bytes/types/link targets are conflicts and never overwritten; identical entries stay, additions merge. Not crash-atomic. Copy changed work to a fresh location and inspect it. Returns {jobId}; poll {action:"status",jobId} or cancel {action:"cancel",jobId}. Successful job.result.destination is the final destination. Jobs belong to this verified owner thread and its subagents; Off and human control apply. Verified subagents use the parent’s Realm; forks have their own. Omit thread overrides, coordinate shared-screen input, and respect Off and human takeover. Realm actions only; ordinary host tools are unaffected, so continue ordinary work.

actions.title: Realm
actions.description: Show this thread's Realm status and open its panel.

settings.label: Desktop size
settings.description: Initial size of new Realms, as WIDTHxHEIGHT.

settings.label: Idle shutdown (minutes)
settings.description: A Realm with no agent or viewer activity stops after this long. Its workspace is kept.

settings.label: Renderer
settings.description: gles2 (GPU) or pixman (software). Use pixman if Realms fail to start on this machine's GPU.

settings.label: Python
settings.description: Python 3.11 or newer on the server, used for the Realm runtime.

settings.label: VM memory (MiB)
settings.description: Guest RAM for new Omarchy VM workspaces (1024–131072). Existing disks retain their launch specification.

settings.label: VM virtual CPUs
settings.description: Virtual CPUs for new Omarchy VM workspaces (1–64).

settings.label: VM virtual disk capacity
settings.description: Capacity for preparing the plugin-local base (16G–2048G). Sparse overlays grow with guest writes; changing this does not resize an existing base.

settings.label: VM unrestricted networking
settings.description: Enabled uses QEMU user networking, including host loopback services through 10.0.2.2. Disabled selects restrict=on and keeps the loopback SSH forward. Applies to new workspaces.

settings.label: Stopped VM disk retention (days)
settings.description: Delete verified stopped VM workspaces unused this many days when listing/starting. 0 keeps indefinitely. Running guests, unknown retirement, open files, shared bases and ISOs are preserved.

settings.label: Omarchy base release
settings.description: Exact stable release for a new reviewed base install. The signed ISO is downloaded only after setup consent. Existing bases/workspaces are preserved.
